timestamp_derivation: The committer date of the last CONTENT commit of this increment, so the receipt cannot describe its own future.
authorisation: Explicit Product-Owner authorisation of 2026-09-23 for exactly two things: ONE controlled end-to-end Guest Device Self-Service acceptance run on PRE-LIVE 172.21.60.25, permitted to temporarily enable only that capability and to update the compiled validation allow-list to admit this appliance through a fail-closed explicit identity check; and Guest-network local-address isolation hardening on PRE-LIVE, implemented in the authoritative generated networking model with fail-safe validation, regression coverage and rollback protection. D41 remains in force. No Guest activation, no Guest pilot, no Go-Live, no PMS-financial or provider traffic, and 172.21.60.23 was not contacted.

what_this_closes.headline: The two technical items that stood between the closure and an unqualified Functional Completeness verdict. Both are proven with live evidence on PRE-LIVE, and both were harder than they looked for reasons the appliance itself supplied.
what_this_closes.device_self_service_acceptance: CLOSED. Proven end to end on PRE-LIVE in a scope-bounded controlled run: pass=36 fail=0, exit 0, appliance verified DARK and restored afterwards. The acceptance establishes that the deployment gate and the per-appliance product setting are two INDEPENDENT controls and that neither alone is enough -- the master flag alone does not mount the guest route; the guest surface without its Phase-3 prerequisite never comes up; with the prerequisite satisfied and the child off the route is still absent; both together mount it. The setting is then consulted per request: OFF tells the guest nothing is available, ON shows their own devices, and turning it off takes effect with no restart. A guest releases their own idle device, exactly one binding remains authorized, an id that is not theirs is refused with NO distinguishing answer, and every outcome including the refusal is in the durable audit. No entitlement outside the reserved stay changed state and no priced purchase exists on the appliance.
what_this_closes.guest_local_address_isolation: CLOSED. A guest network can no longer reach another guest network's appliance-local gateway or portal, nor the management address. Implemented in the authoritative generated model (internal/netcfg/render_nft.go), deployed, and accepted live.
what_this_closes.returned_to_default_off: The capability is OFF and the appliance is DARK, verified by the harness's own restoration checks rather than by assertion: the authoritative flag-coherence gate passes, the guest device route is ABSENT in the running scd (404), the exact DARK Hotel Admin release is current by path and content hash, no live synthetic entitlement/session/device binding remains at the reserved ids, the settings table covers exactly the appliances it did before, and no appliance is left with guest device self-service enabled. Re-confirmed independently after the run and again after a reboot.

the_isolation_boundary.what_was_wrong: The INPUT chain's per-network accepts were keyed on the INGRESS INTERFACE alone -- `iifname "br-g221" tcp dport 8380 accept` -- and the input hook fires for every packet addressed to ANY local address. So a guest on one network reached the appliance on another network's gateway, and on the management address, simply by addressing it. Measured on PRE-LIVE before the change, from a client on VLAN 221: the other network's gateway and the captive portal on it were REACHABLE, and the management address answered ICMP.
the_isolation_boundary.why_the_forward_chain_hid_it: The forward chain already drops guest -> mgmt CIDRs and guest -> @guest_subnets, which is why guest-to-guest client isolation held throughout and was correctly reported as holding. This was the INPUT path to the appliance itself, which those rules never see. That distinction is the whole finding.
the_isolation_boundary.the_fix: Every per-network accept now carries `ip daddr <that network's own gateway>`, plus an explicit boundary drop for @guest_interfaces stated as a rule rather than left to the chain's drop policy -- so that an unconstrained accept appended later is unreachable for guest traffic, which is the safe direction for a future mistake.
the_isolation_boundary.dhcp_keeps_its_broadcast: A client with no address yet sends DISCOVER and REQUEST to 255.255.255.255, so the DHCP accept permits the broadcast destination as well as the gateway. A gateway-only rule there would have broken address assignment outright -- the one mistake available in this change that takes guest networking DOWN rather than hardening it.
the_isolation_boundary.fail_safe_validation: netcfg validate.go already refuses a network whose gateway_ip is not a valid IPv4 address, so such a network cannot be applied at all. The render additionally opens NOTHING for one and says why in the installed ruleset, because an empty address would emit `ip daddr  udp dport ...` and this ruleset is installed as ONE atomic `nft -f` -- a single malformed line does not break one network, it breaks the whole table and takes every guest network with it.
the_isolation_boundary.rollback_protection: netd's existing shape, unchanged and exercised by the acceptance: validate -> apply -> pending_confirmation with an armed watchdog -> confirm, with the health checks that already refuse an apply where Kea cannot bind a guest gateway. The multi-VLAN run reached pending_confirmation with mgmt_reachable, gateway_up, kea_running and portal_listen all true, and was then confirmed active.
the_isolation_boundary.regression_coverage: Six cases in render_nft_guest_input_boundary_test.go, each restriction PAIRED with the path it must not break -- because a ruleset that opened nothing would satisfy 'the other gateway is unreachable' perfectly and take guest internet with it: every guest-bridge accept names its own gateway and not its neighbour's; DNS, the portal and own-gateway ping are still open on each gateway; DHCP still accepts the broadcast destination; a gateway-less network opens nothing, renders no malformed line and says why; the boundary drop exists and sits AFTER the accepts; and the two-NIC management accepts plus both forward-chain drops are untouched.

live_acceptance_after_the_change.tagged_multi_vlan: ALL GREEN, 26 checks, up from 21 because the three results the earlier round could only MEASURE are now ASSERTED and pass. Two tagged VLANs on one trunk, each with its own bridge and gateway, Kea serving both subnets at once with each advertising its OWN option-114 URL, a real DORA on each from its own pool (10.221.0.101 and 10.222.0.101), nftables state for both networks, the revision confirmed active and the management address intact.
live_acceptance_after_the_change.the_boundary_itself: A client on VLAN 221 cannot reach VLAN 222's gateway, cannot reach the portal on it, and cannot reach the management address -- while the portal on its OWN gateway is still reachable and DNS on its own gateway still answers. The Hotel Admin UI, PostgreSQL and SSH remain unreachable from a guest network, and a guest still cannot reach a guest on another network.
live_acceptance_after_the_change.captive_detection: PROVEN, on three separate external addresses: an unauthenticated guest HTTP request to 1.2.3.4, 93.184.216.34 and 203.0.113.9 each returns 200 carrying the portal's own HTML, which is the DNAT redirect delivering the captive portal. A first attempt against a HOSTNAME returned 000 and that was a rig artefact, diagnosed rather than waved away: the guest resolver returns the A record correctly when queried at its own gateway (142.251.209.67), and curl's failure was `Could not resolve host` because the test namespace has no resolv.conf.
live_acceptance_after_the_change.dhcp_dns_portal_walled_garden: A real lease on the production guest network (192.168.77.100), DNS answering A records on its own gateway, the portal answering 200 on its own gateway, and the walled-garden set intact with 1.1.1.1 reachable pre-authentication.
live_acceptance_after_the_change.reboot_and_recovery: A real reboot. All eight services active once settled, the boundary present in the installed ruleset afterwards with no unconstrained guest accept returning, a fresh guest lease, the own portal at 200, the captive redirect at 200, the management address still NOT reachable from a guest, the Phase-6 route still 404, and the admin surface at 200 on login, licence and vouchers. An `admin login -> 502` seen immediately after boot was post-boot settling -- pmsd was still activating -- and it resolved to 200 once the units finished starting; recorded because a 502 that is not explained is indistinguishable from one that matters.

the_harness_could_not_run_here_and_that_.a_hostname_is_not_an_identity: The compiled allow-list was `AUTHORIZED_HOSTS="radius"` -- the retired development appliance -- so the only thing in Phase 6 that can enable a guest capability was admitted by a string any host can be given, while the single host it named must never be contacted. It is now a compiled host -> (appliance_id, serial) map, confirmed against the appliance's SIGNED assignment document and again against its row in the site database, failing closed on a missing entry, a missing file, an unreadable field or any disagreement. Proven to refuse in five ways, each measured. `radius` is removed: a retired host in an enabling allow-list is a standing permission to enable a guest capability on a machine nobody may touch.
the_harness_could_not_run_here_and_that_.two_env_var_bypasses_one_of_them_mine: I first wrote the assignment path as PHASE6_ASSIGNMENT_DOC:-..., which would have been exactly the bypass the file exists to refuse -- an identity check whose SOURCE can be redirected checks whatever the caller points it at. And $COHERENCE, the gate that PROVES the flags went back off, was already PHASE6_COHERENCE:-...: an environment variable that chooses which script answers 'is it dark?' can choose one that always exits 0. Both are fixed paths now.
the_harness_could_not_run_here_and_that_.systemctl_restart_never_returns_here: MEASURED: a run sat in do_wait on `systemctl restart stayconnect-scd stayconnect-acctd stayconnect-edged` for 3 hours 12 minutes during the step that deliberately configures a refusal, and left edged and acctd down for all of it. scd's unit sets Restart=always, RestartSec=2 and StartLimitIntervalSec=0: with the limiter disabled systemd retries the refused start forever, the job never settles, and a synchronous restart waits for a job that cannot finish. The appliance disables the limiter ON PURPOSE so a transient database outage cannot leave a service permanently down -- that policy is right and did not change. The harness had assumed the opposite, and says so in its own comment. restart_units now stops first (which completes, because it cancels the loop), clears the counter, and starts without blocking, with the callers settling on evidence.
the_harness_could_not_run_here_and_that_.and_i_misdiagnosed_it_once: Watching for the run with `pgrep -f 'phase6-controlled-validation.sh run-device-selfservice'` from a shell whose own command line contains that string self-matches, so the watcher could never exit -- and an earlier process listing had already shown that exact class of self-match. A self-excluding `pgrep -af '[p]hase6-...'` identified the real process and the real wait. I then read a transient state during the deliberate fail-closed step as a permanent blocker and said the run could not progress; it had in fact already completed, pass=36 fail=0.
the_harness_could_not_run_here_and_that_.the_body_enabled_more_than_was_authorise: Section 5 validates AGGREGATE ONLINE TIME, a separate Phase-6 child with its own flag, and the authorisation covers only Guest Device Self-Service. The runner gained an explicitly NAMED mode, run-device-selfservice, that stops at that boundary; scope is assigned by the runner from its positional argument and never read from the environment, and the default is full so a caller who forgets the mode runs everything rather than silently less. A matching fault-injection case enables only the authorised capability and then abandons the run.

restoration_was_proven_before_the_body_w: The harness's own rule is that fault injection runs before the real body is ever trusted, and its existing injection cases enable the aggregate flag, so an in-scope case was added. It enabled Device Self-Service, turned the product setting on, seeded synthetic state and abandoned the run: pass=17 fail=0, appliance verified DARK and restored. Restoration also ran twice in one sequence when a hung run was terminated, idempotently, all PASS both times.
what_this_increment_did_not_do: No Guest activation and no Guest pilot: the acceptance is a controlled run with a zero-price administrative grant against reserved identities, and the capability is back OFF. No Go-Live. No real PMS financial posting, payment-provider traffic, settlement or reversal -- all five financial counters remain zero. No change to the two-NIC WAN/LAN architecture and no change to the accepted multi-VLAN behaviour, both asserted by the regression suite. The validation harness was hardened, never weakened, and its allow-list was not replaced by an environment-variable bypass. 172.21.60.23 was not contacted.
go_live: NOT authorised and not performed. D41 remains in force: real Guest activation and Guest pilot use stay DEFERRED. PRE-LIVE remains PRE-LIVE.
